company_name: Franklin Templeton, Inc. (formerly Franklin Resources, Inc.)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K (filed 2025-11-10) cash-flow statement, ShareBasedCompensation add-back $214.8M; no separately disclosed equity-award tax withholding line, so the CF add-back is used as-is (see notes)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 21.11-36.28
inputs.wacc_rationale: Base 10.5%: ~4.2% 10Y UST + ~5.3pp ERP/beta premium for AUM-linked operating leverage to equity/credit markets, PLUS a +1.0pp regulatory single-point-of-failure premium (Western Asset SEC penalty precedent, ongoing criminal proceedings against the former co-CIO -- a concentrated affiliate-level governance risk this multi-boutique model is structurally exposed to repeating). Applied UNIFORMLY across all three scenarios per section 7(f) -- risk is charged once, in the WACC premium and the probability weights (25% bear), never stacked as a higher bear-only WACC on top of an already-conservative bear driver path. Raised from the initial 9.5% after scripts/sanity_check.py flagged wacc_too_low given the cyclicality and regulatory-risk keywords in the qualitative analysis (fix_applied, see sanity_check block).
inputs.lease_treatment: Not material -- BEN's operating lease right-of-use assets ($764.3M) and liabilities ($1,000.6M) are real-estate office leases, immaterial relative to the AUM-fee earnings stream and not separately identified as a lease-cost line in the income statement (folded into occupancy expense, already inside the EBITDA margin build). No separate lease adjustment applied; this is a US operating-company build, not the leases adaptation in section 7(b).
inputs.nci_treatment: Excluded. BEN consolidates Investment Products (CIP) -- seed-capital vehicles and CLOs -- with $12.3bn of CIP investments funded by $9.9bn of CIP debt and $1.18bn of redeemable NCI (mezzanine). These are non-recourse VIE structures, not Franklin's operating business. The model uses COMPANY-ONLY balance-sheet items (cash $3,088.1M, investments $2,374.0M, debt $2,362.0M -- excludes CIP cash/investments/debt entirely) and NetIncomeLoss attributable to Franklin Resources, Inc. ($524.9M FY2025), not consolidated ProfitLoss ($548.9M) which includes CIP/NCI income. This keeps the flow attributable-only and the balance sheet free of VIE noise on both sides simultaneously -- no double count either way.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: Owner-FCF DCF, not a bank/insurer treatment. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md: BEN is an asset manager whose revenue is AUM-based fees and whose free cash flow is a genuine, distributable operating stream -- it holds no deposits (the bank/thrift row does not apply), writes no insurance liabilities (the insurer/BVPS-compounding row does not apply), and is not a REIT or LIC. This is squarely the operating-company owner-FCF row, with the excluded-income/matching-asset adaptation from owner-fcf-adaptations.md section 7(d) applied for its non-operating investment portfolio (analogous to the Japanese cross-shareholding treatment, though BEN is a US filer with no currency adaptation needed). FY0 = FY2025 (fiscal year ended 2025-09-30, 10-K filed 2025-11-10), the last complete audited year; FY2026 is 9 months reported (through 2026-06-30) with record AUM (~$1.8T) but that quarter-level data is not used as the FY0 anchor to avoid mixing a partial year into the base. INVESTMENT INCOME STRIP: 'Investment and other income, net' ($212.8M FY2025 -- dividend/interest income $141.4M, net investment gains/losses -$37.6M, equity-method income $78.0M, FX and other) sits below operating income on BEN's income statement and is genuinely non-operating; it is stripped from owner FCF in full (not just the interest-income sub-line) because operating income itself is already clean of it. The matching asset -- the $2,374.0M company-only investment portfolio -- is added via equity_bridge, per the adaptations rule that every stripped income stream needs its source asset restored. MID-CYCLE MARGIN: statutory operating margin is severely depressed by non-cash intangible impairments tied to the Western Asset outflow scandal and Putnam integration ($226.6M FY2025, $389.2M FY2024, $0 FY2023) -- ex-impairment EBITDA margin was 19.7% FY2023, 14.8% FY2024, 15.5% FY2025. The base case ramps this toward a mid-cycle ~22% as AUM recovers (management guides adjusted operating margin toward 'approaching 30%' by Q4 FY2026 and 29-30% in CY2027 on their own non-GAAP basis, which nets out amortization/impairment more aggressively than this build does -- this model keeps ordinary intangible amortization as a real recurring cost of BEN's serial-acquisition strategy, so its margin ceiling is deliberately below management's own adjusted figure). GROWTH RATE: EPS CAGR is deeply negative over both 3yr (-28.9%) and 5yr (-10.6%) windows -- purely a function of the Western Asset scandal trough (FY2023-25) and is NOT used as the growth proxy; it is a growth_divergence_warning, not a signal to extrapolate. Revenue (3yr 2.0%, 5yr 9.5%) and equity (3yr 1.7%, 5yr 3.6%) CAGRs are used instead, both muted, consistent with a mature, AUM-levered business recovering from a reputational shock rather than compounding. Owner-FCF was roughly flat FY2023-25 (-1.2%/yr on this build's basis) reflecting the trough, not a repeatable growth or decline rate -- the base case growth path is therefore driven by the AUM-recovery and alternatives-mix narrative in the Analysis JSON, not trailing FCF growth. NET CASH: net_debt is -726.1 (net cash) on the company-only basis; net cash does not exceed 1.5x the owner-FCF base so the interest-income-materiality threshold is a closer call, but the strip is applied anyway because operating income is unambiguously already clean of this income and leaving it in would double count against the equity_bridge addition. TERMINAL CAP MULTIPLE: 12x, calibrated to BEN's current EV/EBITDA(ex-impairment) of ~12.1x at the $33.02 price and this sector's typical mid-cycle range (asset managers historically 8-14x EV/EBITDA outside re-rating episodes) -- materially below the 18-20x US-tech default, appropriate for a mature, AUM-beta business with no structural growth premium. SANITY-CHECK FIX (2026-09-26): scripts/sanity_check.py tripped on implied P/E 63.4x vs 10yr average 19.2x (exit code 3). Diagnosis flagged growth_too_high (projected blended ~3.6% vs through-cycle revenue CAGR 1.94%, FY2007-FY2025 first-to-last) and wacc_too_low (cyclicality, regulatory single-point-of-failure keywords in the qualitative analysis). Applied priority-order fixes 2 and 3 (peak-earnings/fix 1 does not apply -- FY0 FY2025 is a scandal trough, not a peak): (a) capped every scenario's growth path so it tapers to at or below the through-cycle CAGR by the outer years rather than sustaining a blended rate above it (base terminal-year growth 2.0% vs cap 1.94%, near enough to be immaterial; the front-loaded 2.5-3.0% reflects only the modelled AUM recovery from the Western Asset trough, which is evidenced by the Analysis JSON's record-AUM/easing-outflows narrative, not an unsupported extrapolation); (b) raised WACC from 9.5% to 10.5% (+1.0pp) for the regulatory single-point-of-failure risk, applied uniformly across scenarios, not stacked per-scenario. Terminal cap multiple (12x base) was left unchanged as it was already calibrated below the current EV/EBITDA(ex-impairment) of ~12.1x and below the US-tech default, so item 4 of the priority order needed no further tightening.

equity_bridge.item: Company-only investment portfolio (seed capital, trading/AFS securities, equity-method investees) -- matching asset for stripped 'Investment and other income, net'
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 10-K balance sheet, 'Investments' line, excludes Consolidated Investment Products (CIP) assets which are non-recourse VIE structures excluded from this model entirely

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGR (3yr -28.9%, 5yr -10.6%) diverges sharply and negatively from revenue (+2.0%/+9.5%) and equity (+1.7%/+3.6%) CAGRs. This is NOT a signal of structural decline: FY2023-25 net income was compressed by the Western Asset Management trade-allocation scandal (>$150bn cumulative outflows since 2024, $100M SEC penalty settled June 2026), Putnam acquisition integration costs, and non-cash intangible impairments ($226.6M FY2025, $389.2M FY2024) tied to AUM writedowns on the affected franchise. Owner FCF (this build's basis) was roughly flat FY2023-25, not growing or shrinking at a repeatable rate. Equity CAGR is used as the conservative growth anchor per the standard selection logic; the base case's near-term growth path is calibrated to the AUM-recovery and margin-normalization narrative in the Analysis JSON (easing Western Asset outflows, record AUM by Q3 FY2026, alternatives/ETF/SMA mix-shift) rather than to any of the trailing CAGRs directly.

base.narrative: Western Asset outflows continue to ease (from >$150bn cumulative since 2024 toward stabilization) without fully reversing; total AUM grows mid-single-digits per year on positive net long-term flows resuming, market appreciation, and the alternatives/ETF/SMA/Canvas platforms continuing to scale faster than the legacy mutual-fund book (record $294bn alternatives AUM, $75.6bn ETF AUM, $30.3bn Canvas, $187.6bn retail SMA per the Analysis JSON). EBITDA margin recovers from the FY2025 trough (15.5% ex-impairment) toward a mid-cycle ~22% as one-off impairment/integration costs roll off and operating leverage from AUM growth flows through, consistent with -- but more conservative than -- management's own adjusted-operating-margin guidance trajectory (approaching 30% by Q4 FY2026, 29-30% in CY2027 on their non-GAAP basis).

bull.narrative: Western Asset outflows fully stabilize and reverse to modest net inflows within 2 years; alternatives fundraising sustains well above the initial $25-30bn target (already tracking ~$40bn for FY2026), ETF/SMA/Canvas platforms compound at 25%+ per year off their small bases, and digital-asset/tokenization initiatives become a genuine third growth leg. Institutional pipeline ($28.6bn unfunded mandates) converts steadily. Operating leverage pushes EBITDA margin to the high-20s%, closer to management's own adjusted-margin target, as Putnam/Western Asset integration synergies are fully realized and no further impairments occur.

bear.narrative: Western Asset outflows reaccelerate or a fresh redemption wave hits another affiliate on reputational contagion; a market drawdown mechanically compresses AUM and fee revenue for 2-3 years while the largely fixed compensation and distribution cost base cannot flex down as fast, compressing margin further before any recovery. The active-to-passive shift accelerates faster than the alternatives/ETF/SMA offset can compensate, keeping the effective fee rate under structural pressure. A further intangible impairment on a legacy affiliate is a realistic outcome in this path, and no re-rating is assumed at exit -- the low 9x terminal cap multiple reflects a chronically discounted, shrinking-AUM active manager.

scenario_narratives.base: AUM stabilizes and grows mid-single-digits as Western Asset outflows continue to ease without fully resolving, alternatives/ETF/SMA platforms keep taking share of the mix, and margin recovers gradually from the FY2025 trough toward a ~22% mid-cycle EBITDA margin as integration costs and impairments roll off.
scenario_narratives.bull: Western Asset fully stabilizes, alternatives/ETF/Canvas/digital-assets growth accelerates well beyond plan, institutional pipeline converts, and operating leverage pushes margin into the high-20s%, closer to management's own long-run target.
scenario_narratives.bear: A fresh redemption wave or market drawdown reaccelerates AUM/fee pressure, the fixed cost base cannot flex down fast enough, a further impairment on a legacy affiliate occurs, and the market never re-rates the stock above a discounted, single-digit terminal multiple.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held above the 15% floor at 25% (bull correspondingly trimmed to 25%, not the 35% default) because BEN carries real single-affiliate concentration risk (Western Asset was ~150bn of cumulative outflows from one scandal) and sits in a structurally challenged industry (active-to-passive fee compression) where a second adverse event is a live, not remote, possibility; the ongoing criminal proceedings against the former Western Asset co-CIO are an unresolved overhang that could reopen reputational damage. This is not going-concern risk -- the balance sheet is net-cash and the credit facility was just expanded/extended to 2031 -- so bear is not pushed to 30-35%, but the asymmetry of a single-customer/single-affiliate blowup case justifies more than the default 15%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Franklin Templeton is valued as an operating company on an owner-FCF DCF, not a bank/insurer/REIT model, because its AUM-based management fees translate into genuine distributable free cash flow with no deposit funding or post-interest AFFO complication. The build strips the company's non-operating investment income (dividend/interest/gains on its seed-capital and CLO-sponsor portfolio) from the FCF base and restores the matching $2,374.0M investment asset in the equity bridge, so that income stream is valued once, at its own balance-sheet value, rather than capitalized twice inside a growing FCF stream. Consolidated Investment Products (CLOs and seed vehicles Franklin must consolidate under VIE rules) are excluded entirely from both the flows and the balance sheet -- they are non-recourse structures substantially funded by third-party debt and redeemable non-controlling interests, not Franklin's economic assets. FY2025 is used as the base year despite being a trough (Western Asset scandal outflows, Putnam integration costs, intangible impairments) because it is the last complete, audited fiscal year; the base case explicitly models recovery from that trough rather than extrapolating either the depressed margin or the flattering record-AUM headline from the unaudited FY2026 interim quarters. A sanity-check pass (scripts/sanity_check.py) tripped on an implied P/E of 63.4x against a 10-year average of 19.2x; the fix raised WACC to 10.5% (+1.0pp for regulatory single-point-of-failure risk) and capped the growth path to taper to the through-cycle revenue CAGR (1.94%, FY2007-2025) by the outer projection years, rather than sustaining a rate above it in perpetuity. See inputs.notes for the full fix record.
key_risks_to_valuation: A second reputational/redemption shock at another affiliate, echoing the Western Asset trade-allocation scandal, given the multi-boutique model's reliance on affiliate-level trust
Structural active-to-passive fee compression continuing to erode the effective fee rate even as AUM grows, capping margin recovery below the base case's ~22% target
AUM's direct exposure to equity/credit market levels -- a market drawdown mechanically cuts fee revenue with a largely fixed compensation/distribution cost base
Further intangible impairments on legacy or acquired affiliates (Putnam, Western Asset) if their AUM bases continue to shrink, which would repeat the FY2024-25 pattern this model treats as a one-off
Integration execution risk across the recent serial acquisitions (Putnam 2024, Lexington 2022, Benefit Street Partners 2019) consuming more management attention and cost than guided
